name: Old Bazaar and Castle Quarter
tagline: The stone heart below the fortress
description: The historic core where cobbled lanes of stone and craft shops climb toward the vast hilltop castle. Full of guesthouses, cafes and Ottoman character, it is the most atmospheric and tourist-facing part of the City of Stone.
bestFor: Culture lovers and short-stay visitors wanting atmosphere, cafes and sights on the doorstep
pros: Castle and museums within walking distance

name: Palorto and Dunavat
tagline: Ottoman tower houses on the slopes
description: The historic residential neighbourhoods spread across the steep hillside, lined with grand grey-roofed tower houses. Quieter and more local than the bazaar, they offer sweeping views over the Drino valley and a genuine sense of old Gjirokaster life.
bestFor: Slow travellers and writers wanting views, calm and authentic old-town living

name: Lower New Town
description: The modern lower town toward the main boulevard, where flatter streets hold everyday shops, supermarkets, banks and cheaper flats. Less picturesque than the old quarter but far more convenient for errands, groceries and comfortable long-term living.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads prioritising affordable flats, easy errands and level walking

name: Drino Valley Outskirts
description: The open outskirts stretching down into the fertile Drino valley, where the town thins into fields, villages and roads toward the Blue Eye and Antigonea. Spacious and rural, it suits those with a car who want quiet and greenery.
bestFor: Drivers seeking space, nature and quiet away from the busy old town
pros: Close to nature and day trips
